Name: Cogapp’s Exhibit
Description: Exhibit (from University of St Andrews): A highly accessible tool that allows users to create interactive presentations. Students can zoom into specific details of a IIIF manifest and add descriptive text. It’s excellent for "close reading" assignments.

Name: Storiiies
Description: Storiiies (by Cogapp): A simple editor for creating annotated tours. It’s very intuitive for students who might not have deep technical backgrounds but want to showcase research on specific image regions.

Name: Annona
Description: A set of web components that can create "storyboards" or "carousels" from IIIF annotations. It’s a great way to turn a list of student-made annotations into a cohesive visual essay.

Name: Liiive
Description: An open-source, web-based tool designed specifically for real-time, collaborative exploration and annotation of IIIF images. Liiive allows you to create shared, in-person annotation assignments.

Name: Recogito (Pelagios Network)
Description: While transitioning through various versions, Recogito remains a powerhouse for semantic annotation. Students can tag places (linking to gazetteers), people, or events directly on the image.

Name: FromThePage
Description: If your assignment involves transcription, this tool uses IIIF to serve images to students while they type out the text. It’s perfect for a "crowdsourced" class project to transcribe a specific historical ledger or letter.

Name: IIIF Curation Platform
Description: A suite of tools from Japan (CODH) that allows for "image cropping" and "curating" specific parts of various manifests into a new, personal collection.

Name: CroppingTool
Description: A freely available tool for cropping details from IIIF images. Croped details can be copied and pasted into disuccion boards or other communication tools.

Name: Anaver.se
Description: A IIIF-enabled online 3D digital exhibit environment.

Name: Mirador
Description: A powerful, customizable viewer ideal for side-by-side comparisons and deep zooming.

Name: Universal Viewer
Description: Simple, clean interface for viewing single or multiple resources.

Name: Tify
Description: A slim, fast viewer that is excellent for looking at large collections or multi-page documents (like digitized books) where the user needs to quickly jump between pages.
